OUR APPROACH

From a good question to better evidence.

An engineering perspective grounded in the work: define the problem, model the system, inspect the result and identify what needs a physical test.

HUMAN-CONTROLLED APPLICATION
Conceptual illustration · not a product image or measured result
Every result should make the next question clearer.
Start with a question that can be tested

A measurement or design objective establishes what needs investigation. In the photonic glucose chip-design example, ArtiSense provides the sensing objective and AIFIELD the engineering workflow.

Keep assumptions attached to the model

Geometry, material conditions, calibration and boundary information shape a simulation result. A model helps investigate the question within those conditions. Its value depends on preserving that context when presenting the result.

Inspect the output with human judgment

The described AI-assisted workflows include proposals and human review. Engineering assumptions and interpretation remain the responsibility of the person conducting the work.

AI workflows
Match the evidence to the claim

A concept describes a direction. A simulation investigates a model. A prototype enables hardware testing. Physical measurement must establish device behavior. The next experiment should address a specific uncertainty.

i

This is a draft explanation based on the supplied work. It does not claim a certified process or completion of every development stage.

A CONNECTED EXAMPLE

One design. Two evidence questions.

How does the design workflow perform? Can the physical system achieve the sensing objective? Explore each in its own context.
